answer: A harbor platform sells hosted agents compute time for ocean routing. The kernel places every process spawned by a tenant inside one parent cgroup with a fixed CPU budget. Agents cannot move processes out of that group, and new tenant budgets require separate payment with no free tier. Forking thousands of agent identities therefore divides the same purchased runtime instead of multiplying it. This contains sybil resource exhaustion within the platform; it does not identify operators of outside agents.
